newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks edge up after four days of losses.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks edge up after four days of losses.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed a fraction higher for the first time in five days but brokers said they were not sure if the correction was over.

The all share index closed 0.31 points higher at 621.93 after easing steadily from 633.5 points on January 27. Price gains edged out declines by 18 to 16. Lanka Orix Leasing rose 1.50 rupees to 152, Korea Ceylon Footwear one to 16.
"I think profit-taking is now over, but buyers are staying out just to see if the index will fall further," said Dimuthu Abeysekera a trader at Allied Phillips Securities.
Turnover was 9.7 million rupees on 406,513 shares. Foreign purchases, supported by 80,000 Lion Brewery, was 4.5 million and sales 2.7 million.
Brokers expect the rest of this week to be thin, with Hong Kong on holiday for the lunar New Year. Hong Kong is Colombo's main source of foreign investment.
Tuesday is Independence day, which is a holiday in Sri Lanka.
